title: Quarter Circle Geometry Task Practice
description: Practice angle, length, and area calculations for a quarter-circle design with chords, tangents, and sectors.

questions.question: A quarter-circle sector has central angle 90 degrees. What fraction of the full circle is the sector?
questions.explanation: A full circle is 360 degrees. Since 90/360 = 1/4, the sector is one-fourth of the circle.

questions.question: A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency.
questions.explanation: The radius to a tangent point forms a 90-degree angle with the tangent.

questions.question: In a quarter-circle design, radii OA and OB form a 90-degree central angle. If chord AB connects the endpoints, what type of triangle is AOB?
questions.explanation: OA and OB are equal radii, and the included angle is 90 degrees, so triangle AOB is an isosceles right triangle.

questions.question: A quarter-circle design has radius 8 cm. Fill in the exact sector area in terms of pi.
questions.explanation: The sector is one-fourth of the full circle: (1/4)pi(8^2) = 16pi.

questions.question: A quarter-circle design has radius 5 cm. What is the exact length of the chord joining the two endpoints of the quarter circle?
questions.explanation: The chord is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 5 and 5, so c = sqrt(5^2 + 5^2) = 5sqrt(2).

questions.question: In the standard quarter-circle endpoint triangle AOB, angle AOB is 90 degrees. Since OA = OB, fill in angle OAB in degrees.
questions.explanation: The two base angles are equal and share the remaining 90 degrees, so each is 45 degrees.

questions.question: For a quarter circle of radius 6 cm, what is the area of triangle AOB formed by the two radii and the endpoint chord?
questions.explanation: Triangle AOB is right with legs 6 and 6, so its area is (1/2)(6)(6) = 18 square centimeters.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain how to find the curved segment area between the chord and arc of a quarter-circle design.
questions.correctAnswer: Find the quarter-sector area, then subtract the area of the right triangle made by the two radii and the chord. For radius r, this is (1/4)pi r^2 - (1/2)r^2.
questions.explanation: The curved segment is the part of the sector left after removing triangle AOB.
